title: Refactor connector abstraction and implement atomic retry commit for async workers
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: We have accumulated ad-hoc connector logic across Redis and Kafka workers: commit semantics are scattered, retry accounting is duplicated, and backpressure signals are inconsistently applied. This causes edge-case double-processing, noisy retry storms during transient infra blips, and makes incremental performance tuning difficult.

Goal: Consolidate connector-level responsibilities into a single async-connector abstraction and introduce an atomic retry-commit primitive so that workers can acknowledge successful work only once all downstream side effects (metrics, KV writes, external API calls) are durably recorded or scheduled. This should reduce duplicate work, make retry budgets enforceable, and provide a clear hook for backpressure and smoothing.

Proposed changes: 1) Create async-connector interface implemented by kafka-consumer and redis-stream adapters that exposes: fetch(batch), mark_committed(batch_id, outcome), and pause_signal(stream_id, reason). 2) Implement an atomic retry-commit flow: work is processed in two phases (execute -> checkpoint). The checkpoint commits offsets/leasing only after a durable commit marker (in Redis or local lease store) is written or an invariant is reached (max idempotency token persisted). 3) Introduce a smoothing window and jittered retry scheduler per connector to avoid bursts when a downstream system recovers. 4) Replace inline backpressure checks with a single circuit-style throttler that exposes pressure state to the connector so it can gracefully slow consumer prefetch. 5) Add observability: per-connector metrics (commits_delayed, duplicate_detected, smoothing_backoff_sec), traces linking fetch->commit, and a dashboard tile in Console for regression detection.

Acceptance criteria: - No increase in end-to-end error rate for existing workloads after rollout. - Duplicate processing rate reduced by >= 95% in synthetic duplicate test. - Observable commit latency under 200ms p95 for normal path. - Retry storms reduced (peak retry rate during simulated downstream outage < 1.5x baseline) and documented playbook.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: Added commit step could increase latency. Mitigation: make checkpoint path configurable; default to async checkpoint with strong idempotency guard and allow sync-only for sensitive queues. - Risk: Migration complexity across clusters. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout per deployment and compatibility shim that falls back to legacy commit behavior.

Rollout plan: 1) Implement abstraction behind feature flag. 2) Run integration tests and internal canary on low-volume tenant pool for 48 hours. 3) Enable smoothing window and throttler in soft-mode (metrics only) for 1 week. 4) Gradual rollout to 25/50/100% with paydown windows, monitoring for duplicate_count and commit_latency.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Async+Connector+Abstraction; initial design notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b_async_connector_notes; dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/async-connector-health
comments: 2026-02-26 - Ava Martinez: Scoped initial spike. Verified we can centralize commit markers into Redis hashes without large memory pressure. Found a potential race when a worker crashes after execute but before checkpoint; will add lease TTL enforcement.

2026-03-01 - Ravi Kapoor: Prototype of connector interface landed in branch feat/async-connector. Basic kafka and redis adapters compile. Added unit tests for mark_committed semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6842
2026-03-03 - Design review (Sana Li): Approved interface shape; asked for clearer failure-mode docs for partial commits and recommended a built-in idempotency token for external API calls.

2026-03-05 - QA (Marcus O): Integration harness created to simulate downstream outages and validate retry smoothing. Early runs show duplicate processing reduced by ~87% — target 95% with additional idempotency guard. Test plan: https://tests.redwood.ai/async-connector-suite

2026-03-08 - Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed for data-in-transit concerns. No secrets stored in commit markers. Suggested KMS-backed signing for idempotency token in high-security queues. Logged as follow-up (ENG-90020).

2026-03-10 - Ravi Kapoor: Implemented smoothing window and added throttler hook. Started 48h canary on tenant pool 'gamma'. Monitoring: no spike in errors; commit_latency p95 ~160ms. Next: validate duplicate_count over 48h and start 25% rollout if stable. Canary dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/canary-gamma-connector
